Workshop | Making Room: A Cyanotype Walk Through the Castro

  • Saturday, October 10, 2026
  • 11:00 AM 1:00 PM 11:00 13:00
  • GLBT Historical Society (map)
  • Google Calendar ICS

LOCATION
GLBT Historical Society Museum
4127 18th Street
San Francisco, CA 94114

ADMISSION
$20 (includes materials fee); Free for GLBT Historical Society Members*

RSVP and reserve tickets here

Inspired by Where We Made Room, this workshop sends you out into the Castro for a walking and blind contour drawing session, capturing the buildings and streets that have held queer life for generations. Back at the museum, we'll trace those sketches onto transparency paper to create negatives, then head outside again to turn them into cyanotype prints using sun print paper—letting the sun fix your drawings into deep Prussian blue.

Just as Landeta's silks layer archival exteriors with imagined interiors to blur document and dream, your prints will hold both what's actually there on the block and the loose, intuitive line your hand found along the way.

No drawing experience necessary, all materials provided. Wear shoes ready for a walk.

*Due to the materials cost for this event, GLBT Historical Society Members are limited for one (1) free ticket to this program.

RESERVE YOUR TICKETS

INSTRUCTOR

Aleo Landeta (they/them) is is a trans and Latine visual artist and educator based in Oakland whose practice spans drawing, painting, installation, and public programming. Their work centers queer joy as liberation, drawing from lived experience and the communities that have held space for them to live authentically. They have been exhibited at MACLA, Bedford Gallery, Berkeley Art Center, and Jonathan Carver Moore, among others, with work held in the permanent collection of the Bakersfield Museum of Art. Recent support includes the SoEx Alternative Exposure Grant (2025), the King Artist Residency (2024), and the Homebody Fellowship at Ma's House & BIPOC Art Studio (2022). Learn More.

Our annual tradition is back! Join us for Reunion 2026, the GLBT Historical Society's gala celebrating LGBTQ+ history and culture and supporting our mission.

Our annual gala brings together hundreds of LGBTQ+ and allied community members from the San Francisco Bay Area and beyond. This year's celebration comes at a crucial time, as the Society works to grow our public programming, expand digital access to our archival holdings, and prepare for our historic move into a new, state-of-the-art home at 2280 Market Street.

Reunion also recognizes the extraordinary contributions of individuals and organizations making a difference to our understanding of LGBTQ+ history and culture and improving the lives of LGBTQ+ community members.
